title: How the material was chosen; creating Red Cross
summary: Grimes sang numbers he had not played in clubs, and he gave Parker the credit for Red Cross.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Charlie Parker: encounters, lore and legacy

blocks.x: Did you select the material for the record date on the spot?

Oh, I'll be damned if I know. I really don't know. When we --- I know Tiny's Tempo was the one that we had got together. Now the singin' ones, Romance without finance, I knew it but I hadn't been doin' it at the club 'cause I didn't sing. I just sang it then. And also the other one, so the singin' ones we did at the station. Because I hadn't been goin' over them in the clubs. I didn't sing, period. So, and then we made up Red Cross, and that was that.
You made Red Cross up there, or were you playing it in the club?

No we weren't playing it in the club, no. I asked him, I said, "look, you got a song you want to do?" and he said "yeah Red Cross." Not being like the fellas are today... greedy... that didn't cross my mind... so I could get all the royalties.
So he had this thing, this first part, and then we got the middle part together, and that was that. I let it go as his song. But it was his song -- just little shit I put in...
